messages.content: Write a contemporary American fiction scene about two adult friends waiting for a bus. Use normal prose and dialogue. Do not use screenplay formatting, character-name labels, stage directions, scene headings, or asterisks around actions. Output only story prose.

The bus was three minutes late, which gave Alex just enough time to become personally offended by it.

“Every bus in this city hates me,” he said.

Jordan looked at the empty road. “It probably has a schedule.”

“A schedule is just a suggestion.”

“That’s not how schedules work.”

“It should be.”

Jordan smiled and pulled her sleeves over her hands. “You said the same thing about your dentist appointment.”

“That was different.”

“You were twenty minutes late.”

“I was emotionally early.”

She laughed. “That doesn't even mean anything.”

“I know.”

A car rolled through the intersection, spraying a thin line of water from the curb. Jordan stepped back without thinking.

“You still have that old photo?” she asked.

“Which one?”

“The one from the camping trip.”

“Oh, God.”

“The one where you fell into the cooler.”

“I did not fall into the cooler.”

“You absolutely fell into the cooler.”

“It tipped over.”

“Because you were sitting on it.”

Alex laughed and shook his head. “I can't believe you still have that picture.”

“I have it framed.”

“You're a terrible friend.”

“I know.”

The bus finally appeared at the far end of the street.

“There,” Jordan said.

Alex straightened. “See? Emotional support works.”
